body:
## Objective
Characterize existing scheduling/review effects and introduce narrow application-owned store capability with adapter using existing owned transaction. Keep command gateway, lock order, receipts, SQLite compatibility, replay and atomic follow-ups intact. Acceptance: no-PG orchestration tests plus native rollback, concurrency, restart and replay parity.

## Coordination
Parent roadmap: #192. Audit baseline: `622d611a2fc6315163a54d7ae689ce1b97d06122`; refresh current main before implementation.

**Full acceptance criteria, non-goals, named regressions, and validation:** [B06 issue specification](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/main/docs/architecture/ci-isolation/issue-specs.md) (section B06).

**Execution constraints:** isolated checkout; protect live study; preserve existing native durability/browser coverage; no merge or deployment without review. Defer until B00/B02 and overlapping outbox/receipt branches reconcile.

Related: [audit report](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/main/docs/architecture/ci-isolation/audit-report.md) · [parallel agent assignments](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/main/docs/architecture/ci-isolation/parallel-impl.md).

comments.body: Reconciliation 2026-10-12: no dedicated B06 extraction PR identified. Merged #172 adds authoritative prepared continuation within the review transaction, while open #191 changes overlapping settlement evidence. These are important behavior/contract prerequisites, not evidence that scheduling-review application orchestration has been extracted behind an owned-transaction port. Keep open pending B00/B02 and #191 reconciliation.

**Source-level finding (main, 2026-10-12):** `backend/app/review_commands.py:52-109` is the worker review handler; line 54 explicitly imports `main._apply_review` (defined `backend/app/main.py:3021-3305`). HTTP `main.py:2955-2997` dispatches `cards.review`/reconcile via `command_dispatch.py:19-77`; `tasks.py:20-26,178-218` registers handlers and executes under foreground admission; `command_gateway.py:229-365` owns operation receipt/transaction/savepoint and post-commit wake. `review_commands.py:16-49,58-108` owns card/queue locks, evidence binding, FSRS call, and optional prepared-head issuance; `_apply_review` owns attempt receipt, schedule, queue status, requeue, priority-refresh enqueue and idempotent replay. This is a **confirmed reverse dependency** worker/application → HTTP composition root. Extract `_apply_review` plus its directly used queue/reconciliation helpers behind an application-owned interface while retaining one gateway-owned PostgreSQL transaction, lock order, prepared continuation, receipts, replay and post-commit wake. Do not merely move route wrappers or split commits. This is code inspection, not runtime qualification.

**Sequencing update:** #217 is the read-only prerequisite for exact transaction/lock/receipt inventory and frozen review interface. #220 separately owns essential queue application extraction; do not combine them into one PR. Review application extraction may start after #217 contract review and #191/#146 conflict assessment. Preserve gateway-owned atomic transaction and prepared continuation. #218/#219 may run concurrently without changing shared contracts.

Architecture audit implications from #217: [complete report and exact extraction contract](https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/blob/076e101474b5227189a98fa280d65c9d80d373fb/docs/architecture/audit-217/REPORT.md#8-204-review-extraction-specification).

The current B06 specification explicitly excludes wholesale `_apply_review` extraction. Preserve that distinction: **A1** introduces the five-capability scheduling store (`source_review_exists`, `load_card_state`, `append_review`, `load_maturity_facts`, `save_card_state`) and typed clock/history/seed inputs, with a same-connection adapter that never commits. **A2**, moving review orchestration and its progression/settings dependencies out of `main`, needs explicit scope reconciliation in #217.

Both contracts preserve gateway transaction/operation receipt ownership, nested reconciliation savepoints, logical receipt replay, evidence completion, optional continuation, locks, and post-commit publication. Keep compatibility wrappers and source-replay behavior; no schema or public interface migration is needed. The report names exact moves/retained functions, rollback, unchanged tests, and additional native/browser qualification. 154 focused Python cases and 13 native proof labels passed on audited main; this is characterization, not qualification of an implementation. This issue remains open and its implementation status is unchanged. Shared interface recommendations are coordinated solely in #217.

Review of completed #217 audit: retain **A1 only** under current B06 scope: same-connection five-capability scheduling store with no commit/receipt ownership. Broader `_apply_review` orchestration removal (A2) requires explicit separately scoped acceptance and dependency review, not implicit expansion of #204. #220 owns queue relocation; #223 owns bounded-work behavior change. #146/#191 and native browser/PG exact-candidate qualification remain dependencies. No implementation status change.

## A1/A2 dependency boundary (2026-10-12)
A1 in this issue is the **five-capability owned-connection scheduling store only**. Broader review orchestration extraction now has a dedicated issue #224 (A2). A1 may be developed independently after its transaction/receipt interface is frozen with #217 and #191/#146 reconciled. Do not move `_apply_review` or queue eligibility/issuance helpers in A1. #220 owns queue application extraction; avoid shared-file concurrent changes or coordinate a single integration owner. A1 completion does not close #224. Keep exact-candidate native PostgreSQL/browser proof requirements.

A1 implementation is available in draft PR #226: https://github.com/aaweaver-actuary/tempo/pull/226.

Source main `3f7332399796366eb32f9fcb5e1b5c678a5b1562`; current head `8200e096d6a2b3475dba34f55c7ff381785be0a0`. Five typed scheduling-store capabilities and the adapter borrowing the existing owned connection are implemented. Wrapper/API/result/source-history behavior stays compatible. `main.py`, gateway, review commands and queue helpers are unchanged. **#224 remains separate and incomplete**; #220 retains queue ownership.

Focused evidence: 23 new controlled cases passed; 218 affected scheduling/replay/continuation/opening/feedback/defense cases passed (61.08s pytest); 81 additional caller/final-import-guard cases passed (12.91s pytest / 13.61s wall); 67 runner tests passed (2.655s).

Fresh native PostgreSQL proofs on current head passed in 31.22s total wall including setup/teardown: `postgres_scheduling_adapter_effects_rollback_with_receipt_failure` and `postgres_scheduling_concurrent_replay_preserves_one_history_and_queue_effect`, plus retained prepared-continuation native lock/head/receipt replay, optional lock decline and edit/deletion issuance fences. The new native tests run through the regular queue-attempt durability hook. Fake-store results do not substitute for these native proofs.

The first complete local durability invocation failed before A1 proofs at unchanged `proof_refresh_state_recovery`: `LockNotAvailable` on `priority_source_epoch` during old-generation completion. 115.91s wall; this is not a durability pass. Original failures are preserved. A first focused native attempt exposed a new-test expectation error (`read_operation` returns state `unknown` for an absent row); only that new assertion was corrected, with a direct row-absence check. No existing expectation/timeout changed.

Browser qualification and fresh exact-candidate FULL CI remain pending; `ci:full` is requested. #146 remains separately conflicted at `6ce1622d...`; #191 advanced to `2940aeff...` with current-main integration and no backend implementation overlap relative to this source main. Their contracts are retained without absorbing their code. No merge/readiness/completion claim.

Live study services and other tasks are untouched. Completed native invocations verified no owned containers/volumes/networks remained; evidence is dated outside the development checkout. Rollback is a revert of A1 commits with unchanged persisted formats. Final qualification/integration SHA and cleanup evidence will be appended here.

title: [CI isolation B06] Isolate scheduling-review application logic behind owned-transaction port
